ପ୍ରଭାକର ଶତପଥୀ

Pravakar Satapathy

The poet’s life

Pravakar Satapathy, born on 15 February 1942, is an Odia poet and editor associated with Jajpur. Singhasan was written during a period when he was active in politics. Its poems draw connections between political life, myth, history and the experience of ordinary people. His literary work spans poetry, magazine editing, and writing about the place of little magazines in literary culture. He previously edited Anisha, participating in the world of small literary publications in which poems, ideas, and new voices find their readers.

His poetry has appeared in Viswamukti, including issues published in 1996 and 1999. His books include the collections Singhasan and Sabuthi Kabita, alongside Sahityare Biplaba O Little Magazine, published in 2014. Together, these works reflect a sustained engagement with both the making of poetry and the spaces that allow literature to circulate. His work has also travelled into Hindi and English: a Hindi selection from Singhasan appears in Sahitya Akademi’s anthology of twentieth-century Odia poetry, while English translations include The Chick and Fear.

Read the poetry archive

Explore the poet’s literary record — books, poems, interviews and public conversations, with links to their sources.

His involvement with readers extends beyond the printed page. In November 2013, he took part in a National Book Trust discussion in Bitana, Jajpur, on promoting reading in rural areas. That occasion belongs to the same literary life as his poems and editorial work: the meeting of books with the communities that read them.

In Singhasan, the throne becomes a way of looking at power across time. Myth and remembered history enter the same field of vision as political ceremony, public spectacle, and ordinary daily life. Crowns, manuscripts, courts, roads, and villages recur in changing relationships; the people who witness authority are as significant as those who claim it.

The collection’s sixty-eight poems form a connected journey. Its opening and closing return to the earth beneath the throne, giving the book a circular movement: what has been buried can be found again, and the old questions can begin anew. Read together, the poems invite attention to the distance between grandeur and lived experience, and to the persistence of everyday life around the symbols of rule.

Pravakar Satapathy lives and breathes poetry. It lights up his face, finds expression in his gestures, and flows into conversation.

He loves meeting people and talking about poems, memories and life. If you’re in Bhubaneswar, he would be happy to welcome you for a conversation. Get in touch with his family to arrange a visit—you don’t have to be a poet to share a love of poetry.

ଆମ ଘର

Read the poem

ଡାକିଲି :ଆ, ଘରକୁ ଆ,
ମୋ ଘରକୁ,
ଏବେ, ଏଇ ମୁହୂର୍ତ୍ତରେ.
:ନା ଏବେ ନୁହେଁ,
ଦେଖିବା ଆଉ କେବେ.

ସେ ଡରୁଥିଲା
ନା ସୁରକ୍ଷା ଖୋଜୁଥିଲା?

ସେ ସତରେ ନଥିଲା,
ନିଜ ଭିତରେ ନଥିଲା,
ଡରୁଥିଲା ଡରକୁ,
ନିଜକୁ
ସାମ୍ନାରେ ଠିଆହୋଇ
ଧୀରେ ପାଦ ବଢ଼ାଇଲି ଆଗକୁ.
ସେ ଧରିପକାଇଲା ହାତ
ପାଦରେ ପାଦ ମିଳାଇ ଚାଲିଲା ସାଥିରେ,
ଚାହିଁଲା ଆକାଶକୁ
କହିଲା :
ତୋ ଘର ନୁହେଁ,
ମୋ ଘର ନୁହେଁ,
ଚାଲ,
ଚାଲୁ ଚାଲୁ ମହାଶୂନ୍ୟରେ
ରଚିଦେବା ଘର,
ନୂଆ ଏକ ଘର,
ଆମ ଘର.

ମୋ କବିତା

ନା ସେ ଛାଡୁଛି

ମୋ ନାଭିମଂଡଳରେ ସେ ବସାବାଂଧୁଛି।
ଯେତେ ଭାବୁଛି ବୁଝିବି ତାକୁ
ଝାଳଦେଇ
